S68.01.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, with at least one cloud session
S68.01.note: No session ID is shown on the screens read, so the tester compares title and repository. The button that opens the side menu was not checked.
steps: Sign in on the phone, open the side menu and tap "AGI Code".
Note the title and repository of one session in the "Sessions" list.
On a second client (web app or desktop app) signed in to the same account, find the session with the same title.
Compare: both clients should show the same session with the same title and repository, not a copy.
S68.01.where: AGI Code > Sessions list (tap a session row)

labels.text: Earlier turns of this session are not shown here.

S68.02.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, with a session that has several turns
S68.02.note: The phone can show a notice that earlier turns are not shown, so the history may be cut short by design.
steps: Open AGI Code and tap a session.
Scroll the transcript up to the oldest turn.
On the second client, open the same session.
Compare the turns: both should show the same conversation history.
S68.02.where: AGI Code > tap a session row

S68.03.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, with a session that has a working branch
S68.03.note: The branch appears in the workspace line built by cloudCodeWorkspaceLabel; the exact text format was not confirmed on screen.
steps: Open AGI Code and tap a session.
Read the small line under the session title, which shows the workspace (repository and branch).
Tap the "Changes" button in the session header (git-branch icon) to open the changes sheet.
Compare the branch with the branch shown on the second client for the same session.
S68.03.where: AGI Code > tap a session > small line under the session title, then the Changes button

S68.04.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, with a session linked to a repository
S68.04.note: Sessions without a repository go under the heading "No repository" (presentation.ts).
steps: Open AGI Code.
Tap the sort button at the top right (its label starts with "View and sort sessions").
Tick "Group by repository".
Check that the list is split into sections named by repository, and that the session sits under the same repository as on the second client.
S68.04.where: AGI Code > View and sort sessions button > Group by repository

S68.06.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, with a cloud session
S68.06.note: The model name is shown on the composer line. No visible instruction-file setting was found in the mobile cloud session screens (searched apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code and companion for "instruction").
steps: Open a session in AGI Code.
Read the line under the message box that shows the model name and, when known, the context percentage.
Tap "Task options and usage" and read the "Task options" sheet (Mode and Usage).
Compare the model with the second client for the same session.
S68.06.where: AGI Code > tap a session > Task options and usage

S68.08.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, and a task that asks for an approval
S68.08.note: The session reloads about every 4 seconds while a turn runs (CLOUD_CODE_SESSION_POLL_INTERVAL_MS in useCloudCodeSession.ts), so the card can take a few seconds to show.
steps: Start a task on the second client (desktop or web) that needs a tool approval.
On the phone, open AGI Code and that session.
Look for the "Approval required" card in the session with its approve and reject buttons.
Tap approve on the phone and check that the approval card clears on the second client.
S68.08.where: AGI Code > open a session that is waiting for approval

labels.text: Describe a task or ask a question

S68.09.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, and a task that runs tools
S68.09.note: The phone reloads the session about every 4 seconds while a turn runs, so activity may appear with a short delay.
steps: Open the same session on the phone and on a second client, side by side.
On the phone, type a task in the box that says "Describe a task or ask a question" and send it.
Watch the "Working" row on the phone and on the second client.
Look for tool activity lines such as "Ran a command" on both clients.
S68.09.where: AGI Code > open a session > type in the message box and send

S68.11.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, and a task that is still running
S68.11.note: Send, stop and approve use the same composer and approval card, so one client can drive the session the same way as the other.
steps: Send a task that runs for a while.
Open the same session on the phone while it is running.
Check that the composer shows the "Stop the task" control, and that a pending approval can be answered from the phone.
Tap "Stop the task" and watch the label change to "Stopping the task"; check the second client shows the same change.
S68.11.where: AGI Code > open a running session > Stop the task

S68.14.needs: a paired desktop computer with its sessions running locally
S68.14.note: The remote screens (companion index and companion code thread) show "Remote" as unavailable in this build, because FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts. The computer session list in AGI Code (useComputerCodeSessions) was not traced to a visible control that continues a local session.

S68.19.needs: a paired desktop, CLI or VS Code client on the same account
S68.19.note: The "Devices" heading (CodeDevicesSection.tsx) and the "Your computers" card (AccountComputersCard.tsx) both return nothing while FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts, so they are not visible in this build.

S68.20.needs: a paired desktop, CLI or VS Code client on the same account
S68.20.note: The card is titled "Your computers" and shows presence as Online, Asleep or Offline (PRESENCE_LABELS in AccountComputersCard.tsx), but it is hidden while FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts.

S68.21.needs: a paired desktop with its capabilities set
S68.21.note: Capability names are Remote control, Browser, Computer use, Local models and Local MCP (CAPABILITY_LABELS in AccountComputersCard.tsx). The card is hidden while FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts.

S68.22.needs: a computer with AGI Desktop open, and a phone with camera access for the QR code
S68.22.note: Pairing controls exist ("Add device" in packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts, "Pair with Desktop" and "Scan QR Code" in ConnectionStateViews.tsx), but all are hidden while FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts.

S68.23.needs: a paired desktop and a phone that is paired with it
S68.23.note: The phone side is the "Disconnect" button in DesktopInfoCard.tsx with a confirmation alert in companion/index.tsx, but both are hidden while FEATURES.companion is false. The desktop side was not checked.

S68.25.needs: a paired desktop that can be put to sleep or closed
S68.25.note: The text "is offline" and the explanation about remote access stopping are in companion/code/[threadId].tsx, but that screen shows "Remote" as unavailable while FEATURES.companion is false in apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts.

S68.26.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, and a running session
S68.26.note: This covers only the cloud session reloading when the app returns to the front (AppState listener in useCloudCodeSession.ts). The desktop reconnect screen ("Reconnecting to" in companion/code/[threadId].tsx) is hidden while FEATURES.companion is false.
steps: Open AGI Code and tap a session.
Switch away from AGI Mobile or lock the phone for a short while, and start a new turn on the second client for the same session.
Come back to AGI Mobile without reopening the session.
Check that the session shows the new turns and state.
S68.26.where: Effect seen on an open AGI Code session after the app comes back to the front

S68.30.needs: a second client signed in to the same account, push notifications allowed for AGI Mobile on the phone
S68.30.note: The notification titles come from apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts, and the push is triggered by apps/web/app/api/code/local-sessions/activity/route.ts. The tester needs a second client to produce the activity. The reach of the notification settings from the main Settings screen was not confirmed.
steps: Sign in on the phone, open the side menu and tap "AGI Work".
Tap "Open notification settings" and check that "Task and approval updates" is on. Its description reads "Approval requests and finished or failed tasks".
On a second client, start a cloud session task that needs approval or finishes.
Check the phone shows a notification titled "Approval needed", "Agent run finished" or "Agent run failed".
S68.30.where: AGI Work > Open notification settings > Task and approval updates
